output.normalized_title: redis-cluster: DNS resolution timeout on route53 (redis-cluster)

output.classification_reasoning: The incident is centered on a DNS resolution timeout from Route53, which is a network-level service used by the redis-cluster for name resolution. The symptom set (DNS timeout and a secondary telemetry spike) points to a failure in the network/DNS path rather than an application bug, authentication problem, or storage/database exhaustion. Resolving such an issue typically involves tracing DNS queries, checking Route53 health, and verifying network connectivity between the client and the DNS service, which adds a layer of external dependency. This external dependency and the need to coordinate across DNS and networking components elevate the effort beyond a simple local misconfiguration, but it does not require deep multi‑service root‑cause analysis, placing the incident at a moderate level of operational complexity.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has the required ProdOperations role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us‑east‑1.
verification: Node list returns only production nodes

remediation_steps.title: Enforce Write‑Freeze on Redis Cluster
remediation_steps.description: Prevent any new write traffic while remediation proceeds to avoid data inconsistency.
commands: kubectl -n redis exec deployment/redis-primary -- redis-cli CONFIG SET protected-mode yes

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary
remediation_steps.description: Elevate the healthy read‑replica to become the new primary before tearing down the failing node.
commands: kubectl -n redis exec deployment/redis-replica-0 -- redis-cli replicaof no one
verification: Write test: redis-cli -h <new-primary-endpoint> SET test_key "ok" succeeds

remediation_steps.title: Reboot Affected Redis Node
remediation_steps.description: Perform a controlled reboot of the failing EC2 instance hosting the old primary to clear the network stack.
commands: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-0abcd1234efgh5678 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters commands=['sudo reboot'] --region us-east-1
verification: aws ec2 describe-instance-status --instance-ids i-0abcd1234efgh5678 shows status checks passed
kubectl get pods -n redis -l app=redis | grep -i terminating returns no results
DNS lookup for redis-cluster.internal resolves to the new primary IP

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Confirm the cluster is healthy, DNS resolves correctly, and no error signatures appear in logs.
commands: kubectl -n redis logs deployment/redis-primary | grep ERR_NETWORK_FAILURE_370 || true
verification: Log grep returns no matches for ERR_NETWORK_FAILURE_370
All redis pods show READY=1/1 and STATUS=Running

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert the promotion, restore the original primary node image, and re‑enable writes. Each step includes verification before proceeding to the next.

commands: kubectl -n redis exec deployment/redis-primary -- redis-cli replicaof <old-primary-ip> 6379
verification: Write test against old primary succeeds

steps.description: Rollback Deployment Image to Pre‑Change Tag

commands: kubectl -n redis exec deployment/redis-primary -- redis-cli CONFIG SET protected-mode no
kubectl -n redis logs deployment/redis-primary | grep ERR_NETWORK_FAILURE_370 || true
verification: No error signatures appear in logs for 5 minutes
